scope: Caller-string access during exFAT matching in HackScsd_FindFile, src/hack_scsd.c
finding: The comparison kept indexing the requested name after detecting its terminator or an earlier mismatch, potentially reading beyond its allocation when the on-disk name was longer.
change: Stop reading requested-name characters after mismatch while still consuming directory fragments. Reject NULL names before exFAT traversal; FAT short-name paths retain their existing behavior.
verification: check_scsd_exfat_names.py executes the production lookup with only requested-name reads instrumented to check the exact NUL-terminated extent
All 0..255 on-disk/requested lengths, matching/case-folded, first-character mismatch and non-ASCII UTF16 mismatch (196608 cases)
Cross-sector filename fragments, final length equality, unchanged failed-match metadata and NULL early rejection verified
Baseline b381a97 fails the same fixture; current source passes
Existing FAT-directory and cluster-address checks pass; GNU ARM compilation passes without diagnostics
limitations: Controlled directory sectors and string-access instrumentation, not a physical-memory sanitizer or SD hardware. Entry checksums/sequence validity, directory attributes, 64-bit file lengths, Unicode filename support and full native transport remain unverified.
